Two randomised head-to-head trials do exist, in other settings, and this page said they did not.
Both put ribociclib against palbociclib.

Shaaban and colleagues randomised patients to palbociclib plus fulvestrant or ribociclib plus fulvestrant in the second line and reported a clinical benefit rate at six months of 58.6% in both arms and median progression-free survival of 12.69 against 13.67 months; their conclusion, in their words, is that both Ribociclib and palbociclib have similar CBR, PFS and toxicity profile .
HARMONIA (NCT05207709) is a phase III, randomised, open-label trial of the same pair in the HER2-enriched subtype; it opened in March 2022 and terminated with 61 patients enrolled.
Neither is first line with an aromatase inhibitor, which is why neither contradicts the guideline sentence.
Both contradict what this page printed, which was that nobody had run one at all.

What they do not do is close the abemaciclib question: no randomised trial has compared abemaciclib against either of the other two , in any setting, and that is the comparison the category difference actually turns on.

Two exist, both of ribociclib against palbociclib: a randomised open-label phase III in the second line with fulvestrant, published in 2024, which found no difference between them; and HARMONIA, registered as NCT05207709, which opened in March 2022 and terminated with 61 patients.

Shaaban and colleagues randomised 116 patients - 58 to each arm, in blocks of four by sealed envelope, at a single centre in Egypt - to palbociclib plus fulvestrant or ribociclib plus fulvestrant in the second line.
Clinical benefit at six months was 58.6% in both arms, exactly 34 patients of 58 either way.

Median progression-free survival was 13.67 months on palbociclib against 12.69 on ribociclib, and not significantly different - though progression-free survival was a secondary endpoint there, the trial being powered on response rate.
Their conclusion, in their words: both Ribociclib and palbociclib have similar CBR, PFS and toxicity profile .

Source of the 116 patients and the 58 per arm, the randomisation in 29 blocks of four by opaque sealed envelope, the clinical benefit rate at six months of 58.6% in both arms (34 of 58 either way), the median progression-free survival of 13.67 months on palbociclib against 12.69 on ribociclib, and the authors' conclusion that both Ribociclib and palbociclib have similar CBR, PFS and toxicity profile .
